source.title: SafeConstellations: Mitigating Over-Refusals in LLMs Through Task-Aware Representation Steering
source.authors: Utsav Maskey; Sumit Yadav; M. Dras; Usman Naseem

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study contrasts task-conditioned representation trajectories and steering with a global, task-agnostic direction, and reports its own geometry and intervention results. This refines the single-direction account, but it does not reproduce the original difference-in-means ablation or addition experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper constructs task-specific target-minus-refusal centroids and uses them for selective activation steering. It reports over-refusal rates and task-conditioned cluster-separation results. It does not remove or add the original harmful-minus-harmless direction, edit weights, test jailbreak suppression of that direction, or test reasoning models. Values used to select layers and hyperparameters are not recorded as outcomes. Related plots are recorded only where the text explicitly describes their result.
record.test_reason: This is an over-refusal mitigation paper. It steers with per-task centroid differences (non-refusal minus refusal outcomes on benign-task prompts) and reports only its own method's over-refusal and MMLU numbers across ablations. It never builds, ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless direction (V1). It does not count or characterise refusal directions (V4). It runs no weight edit, jailbreak, harm-vs-refusal, transfer, training or reasoning-model test. Silhouette scores measure how well target and over-refusal outputs separate, not refusal-direction geometry. The global fixed-layer steering also cut over-refusal by 60%, so the study does not show a single direction failing.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Precisely: the authors conclude that task identity is the main organizer of layer-wise trajectories, and that over-refusal varies by task. Task-gated, trajectory-aware steering reduces over-refusal with minimal utility loss while preserving refusals of harmful inputs. They contrast this with prior single global steering, saying the non-refusal direction is ambiguous when tasks are combined. They do not empirically test a global direction's failure.
record.recipe_differences: Uses per-task target and refusal centroids, selects a few task-dependent layers, and adds a scaled task-specific steering vector at inference time. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless direction or project it out across all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with task and steering configuration: task-specific steering, trajectory modulation, layer selection, and fixed versus dynamic layers produce different over-refusal rates; task-specific silhouette scores differ from the combined setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Target vs over-refusal embeddings for benign-task prompts separate better within a task than pooled. LLaMA-3.1-8B silhouette: sentiment 0.119–0.158 and translation 0.133–0.143, vs combined 0.077–0.102 at L12–L20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representations separating refusal from compliance on benign-task prompts are task-conditioned (outcome-based separability, not harmful-vs-harmless direction geometry).

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a task-specific non-refusal-minus-refusal centroid vector at a few layers reduces over-refusal (LLaMA 17.77→4.81%, Qwen 8.15→2.96%) with no MMLU loss. Non-task-specific intense fixed-layer steering also reduces it (7.03%) but costs MMLU (43.66) and coherence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Outcome-based difference-in-means steering can reduce over-refusal; task conditioning preserves utility better than a fixed global vector.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), as stated in the supplied metadata and paper references.
record.problems: The study does not test the original single-direction intervention or directly measure how many directions are required. Its geometry evidence is partly visual, and silhouette scores do not establish direction dimensionality. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Utility preservation is evaluated primarily with MMLU; the paper notes this does not assess factuality, coherence, calibration, or long-context robustness.
record.rows_left_out: No additional applicable numeric findings left out. Utility/MMLU values were not added as rows because they do not measure V4's representation-geometry claim; cited findings from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless direction, no ablation or addition of it, no refusal induction on harmless prompts.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial-training test.
No count of refusal directions; no affine, cone or dominant-plus-secondary analysis; no test that a single global direction fails to mediate refusal.
No separate harm and refusal representations.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer. Task embeddings are stated not to transfer across models.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T5 to uses_without_test/T4; all rows are unlinked, and the reader's V4 labels are removed. The study cites Arditi et al. only as related steering work. Its 'refusal' cluster is defined by response outcome on benign-intent prompts, not by harmful vs harmless instructions. Judge is GPT-4o. No uncertainty is reported. The 270-sample test set includes only 48 (LLaMA) and 22 (Qwen) over-refusal cases.

versions.untested_parts: No intervention with the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction; no projection out at every layer and position; no inducing refusal on harmless prompts with that direction.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
No test of whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.

The study tests task-conditioned representation patterns and interventions, but does not test affine or cone geometry explicitly, establish the number of independent directions, or compare a dominant direction plus residual directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision as encoded representations.
Models are analyzed separately; task embeddings are stated not to transfer between models. No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or transferred-direction experiment.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages to determine when a removable direction exists.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Task-specific embedding separation and task-specific steering outcomes support the paper's refinement that refusal-related representation patterns vary by task rather than being adequately captured by one global task-agnostic pattern (r1-r20, r26-r27). The silhouette metric itself does not establish direction count.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The combined-setting silhouette scores are lower than the task-specific sentiment and translation scores at the reported layers, and the paper describes the combined trajectory as ambiguous; this supports task dependence but does not establish a specific affine, cone, or multiple-direction geometry (r21-r25, r26).
